stories.title: Attack in Niger State's Borgu LGA sparks deadly reprisals
stories.body: Suspected terrorists attacked Lumman-Ba'are and Gada-Oli communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State, at dawn on 21 November. Police confirmed about five deaths; local reports put the toll at 11 or more, including a village head and his family. Kambari militias then attacked Fulani residents and refugees in nearby villages including Wawa, where eyewitnesses counted about 20 bodies. The total death toll is unconfirmed.
stories.why: Revenge attacks along ethnic lines can turn a single terror raid into wider communal violence, a pattern seen across the North-central.

cards.front: Which Niger State LGA saw a terror attack and reprisal killings on 21 November 2026?

stories.title: Three killed in Gombe community; residents blame Air Force personnel
stories.body: Three people died and 13 were injured in Lawanti community, Akko LGA, Gombe State, on the night of 20 November. Residents allege that personnel of the Nigerian Air Force's 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group shot and beat people during a row over suspected theft of armoured cables. The Air Force did not respond, and the causes of death are not established. Governor Inuwa Yahaya ordered an investigation.
stories.why: Alleged abuses by security forces against civilians damage public trust, which intelligence and security work depends on.

stories.title: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
stories.body: At a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin on 19 November, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia is comfortable with post-war security guarantees for Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5, and that President Trump is open to the idea. President Putin has called NATO membership or NATO guarantees for Ukraine unacceptable. President Zelenskyy said there was no common understanding of what such guarantees would mean, and no details have been agreed.
stories.why: Security guarantees are the main condition Ukraine sets for any ceasefire deal.

cards.back: The collective defence clause: an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all.

stories.title: US warns ships against ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian oil
stories.body: US Central Command said on 18 November that ships taking cargo from blockaded vessels loaded at Iranian ports could be stopped, boarded or captured. The US first imposed its naval blockade on 13 April, lifted it in June and reinstated it on 14 July. Reuters reported a tanker loading Iranian crude by ship-to-ship transfer in the Gulf, which would be the first successful export since July; Iran has not confirmed this. Oil is around 30 percent of Iran's economy.
stories.why: The blockade keeps Iranian oil off the market, which helps hold world oil prices up.

cards.front: When did the US reinstate its naval blockade of Iran?
cards.back: 14 July 2026, after a June understanding with Tehran collapsed. It was first imposed on 13 April.

stories.title: Inflation falls to 14.06 percent, but prices still rising
stories.body: The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation fell to 14.06 percent in October 2026, from 14.63 percent in September and 18.97 percent a year earlier. Food inflation was 19.13 percent. Month on month, prices rose 0.43 percent, up from 0.06 percent in September. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said falling inflation does not mean falling prices, only that prices are rising more slowly.
stories.why: Knowing the latest inflation figure, and the difference between inflation and prices, is a common economy question.

cards.front: What was Nigeria's headline inflation in October 2026 (NBS)?
cards.back: 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September.

cards.front: Does falling inflation mean prices are falling?
cards.back: No. It means prices are rising more slowly. Falling prices is called deflation.

stories.title: Trump: 'We don't need a deal with Iran'
stories.body: President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice-President Vance, who had led negotiations, to focus on domestic issues. Secretary of State Rubio said economic pressure on Iran is working and will get worse, so large-scale military operations are unnecessary. Iran says it has sent a seven-condition proposal through Qatar and that the ball is in the US court. On the same day, Iran claimed it struck a US radar site in Bahrain; the US said it shot down two Iranian drones and nothing was damaged.
stories.why: A long 'no war, no peace' stand-off keeps Hormuz disrupted and oil prices high, which shapes Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs.

cards.front: How did Chatham House describe the US–Iran situation in November 2026?
cards.back: "No war, no peace": neither a deal nor full-scale fighting.
